why: Author names the EIP deliberately; residual error is a blocker or changelog mention, ~5-in-8 precision
A fix touching a fork-config or reference-test file inherits every EIP that file lists: 0 of 14 reviewed matches were real
Generic names collide (process_block, get_ancestor are ordinary methods) and presence is not aboutness: 11 of 11 sampled anchors contaminated over 122 records
Removes file-level inheritance but spec functions call each other, so a focused fix touches several; at a 1-anchor cap it yields 7.0% and 20 anchors, worse than prose on both
Structural types are ubiquitous in consensus code (BeaconState in 146 records) and collide across domains (Checkpoint matched Polygon Bor's unrelated checkpoint type)
Network preset and config files enumerate every constant with its value, so two lodestar preset records manufacture the multi-client status of dozens of constants
